simple.meaning: אָזַן (ʼâzan) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to broaden out the ear (with the hand), i.e. (by implication) to listen.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 41 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges, and 9 more, beginning at Genesis 4:23. Its contexts include commandment, kingship, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָזַן (H238).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָזַן (ʼâzan) / H238 is traced through Genesis 4:23, Exodus 15:26, Numbers 23:18, Deuteronomy 1:45 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Lamech said to his wives,

He said, “If you will diligently listen to Yahweh your God’s voice, and will do that which is right in his eyes, and will pay attention to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you, which I have put on the Egyptians; for I am Yahweh who heals you.”
He took up his parable, and said,
You returned and wept before Yahweh; but Yahweh didn’t listen to your voice, nor turn his ear to you.
Give ear, you heavens, and I will speak.
“Hear, you kings!
Yet he sent prophets to them, to bring them again to Yahweh, and they testified against them; but they would not listen.
Yet many years you put up with them, and testified against them by your Spirit through your prophets. Yet they would not listen. Therefore you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
If I had called, and he had answered me,
“Behold, I waited for your words,
“However, Job, please hear my speech,
“Hear my words, you wise men.
“If now you have understanding, hear this.
“Listen to this, Job.
Listen to the voice of my cry, my King and my God;
Hear, Yahweh, my righteous plea;
Oh spare me, that I may recover strength,
both low and high,
Behold, God is my helper.
Attend to me, and answer me.
